sub_answers.sub_question: What approximation errors arise from basis truncation or finite-mode representations in manifold-decomposition models?
sub_answers.text: Truncating bases or using finite-mode representations introduces approximation error from low-rank matrix approximation that omits residual subspace dynamics [d122523s0p0]. [d104494s0p0] Reduced-order models based on proper orthogonal decomposition can fail to represent branching or bifurcating solution components when the reduced basis lacks modes for those branches [d104494s0p0]. [d122523s0p0] Projection-based residuals capture uncertainties arising from omitted modes and propagate through detection or estimation via matrix perturbation effects [d122523s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How does mismatch between assumed manifold (e.g., isotropic sphere) and real propagation environments affect model accuracy?
sub_answers.text: Assuming isotropic or otherwise simplified manifolds when the real environment is non-isotropic causes errors in second-order statistics and time-varying mutual information characterizations under Rayleigh fading [d140424s0p0]. [d130716s0p0] Mismatches between assumed steering manifolds and actual waveform-induced phase errors produce degraded beamforming, direction finding errors, and increased sidelobe levels [d130716s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What trade-offs exist between model generality (array independence) and the fidelity of array-specific phenomena like mutual coupling?
sub_answers.text: Array-independent, general models trade physical fidelity for applicability by not modeling array-specific phenomena such as coupling between elements [d73987s0p0]. [d73987s0p0] High-fidelity treatment of mutual coupling requires including coupled-waveguide or element interaction physics, which increases model complexity and reduces generality [d73987s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How sensitive are array-independent models to measurement noise, limited angular resolution, and finite sample effects?
sub_answers.text: Array-independent approaches are sensitive to finite-sample effects because residual subspaces capture uncertainties that grow under matrix perturbation and limited data [d122523s0p0]. [d140424s0p0] Measurement noise and low SNR change second-order statistics and degrade accuracy, with different approximations required in low- and high-SNR regimes [d140424s0p0]. [d70453s0p0] Models trained under one distribution can suffer task mismatch and reduced performance when testing environments or angular resolution differ from training, especially in non-stationary scenarios [d70453s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How can array-independent channel representations simplify antenna design optimization and port/element placement decisions?
sub_answers.text:
Characterizing geometry with aperture-level metrics like a geometric inertia matrix makes port placement decisions directly linked to estimation precision via Cramér–Rao bounds, simplifying placement trade-offs [d124158s0p0].
Movable and rotatable antenna elements create explicit geometry and orientation degrees of freedom that let designers treat placement and boresight direction as optimization variables rather than fixed constraints [d122101s0p0][d122979s0p0].
Closed-form characterizations of inter-port distance statistics for planar apertures provide simple scaling laws that guide how many candidate ports can be packed and where to place them for favorable geometry diversity [d124158s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: In what ways do manifold-based models affect MIMO precoding, beamforming, and capacity prediction?
sub_answers.text:
Including orientation or reconfigurable-geometry manifolds in channel models enables joint optimization of transmit covariance and element orientations, which in turn lets precoding adopt eigenmode transmission with water-filling tuned to the engineered channel [d122979s0p0].
Manifold-aware design supports beamforming and artificial-noise covariance optimization under geometry constraints to maximize sum rate or secrecy, integrating placement and beamformer design into a single problem [d122101s0p0].
Optimizing scattering- or manifold-parameterized surfaces permits fractional-programming and manifold-optimization based base-station beamforming that leverages the engineered equivalent channel for improved capacity prediction and BF performance [d123865s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How are channel estimation and measurement procedures adapted when using array-independent manifold decompositions?
sub_answers.text:
Array-independent manifold decompositions make estimation precision depend on a geometric inertia matrix, so elevation–azimuth joint estimation and CRBs are computed from aperture geometry rather than array-specific element responses [d124158s0p0].
Design choices that maximize geometric determinants to reduce CRBs must balance increased sidelobe-induced ambiguity, indicating channel measurement procedures must account for precision–ambiguity trade-offs in port placement [d124158s0p0].
When elements or surfaces are reconfigurable, channel measurement and estimation workflows include joint optimization of element positions and phase shifts using algorithmic solvers such as particle-swarm, SDR, or MMSE-based methods for improved channel reconstruction [d105691s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What computational or implementation benefits do array-independent models provide for large MIMO or massive MIMO systems?
sub_answers.text:
Array-independent models enable algorithmic decompositions and low-dimensional parameterizations that reduce online optimization complexity, as evidenced by alternating optimization and manifold-based solvers for orientation and covariance that converge rapidly [d122979s0p0][d122101s0p0].
Data-driven precoding that learns mappings from channel matrices to precoders can cut online computation for large MIMO systems by shifting complexity to offline training [d71672s0p0].
Hardware-aware transmission strategies such as constant-envelope precoding and antenna grouping reduce RF-chain and power-amplifier complexity for large arrays while remaining compatible with geometry-aware models [d32544s0p0].
Analytic and linear methods for DoF and SDoF bounds provide closed-form or efficiently solvable formulations that scale to many-antenna configurations and guide element allocation for interference and leakage cancellation [d110116s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What is manifold decomposition in the context of wireless channel modeling?
What defines an array-independent channel model versus an array-dependent model?
sub_answers.text: An analytic array model requires perfect array geometry information to produce its response predictions [d97529s0p0]. A learned array response model can be obtained from calibration data and captures the characteristics of transducers and array behavior without relying on perfect geometry knowledge [d97529s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How is MIMO scattering traditionally represented in physics-based channel models?
sub_answers.text: MIMO scattering is represented in terms of angular spread and array dimensions to determine degrees of freedom in the channel [d16930s0p0]. Scattering is modeled as either uncorrelated (leading to linear growth of degrees of freedom with array size) or as colored/correlated scattering that can limit degrees of freedom and cause saturation for large arrays [d16930s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Which mathematical spaces or bases are commonly used to represent propagation manifolds (e.g., spherical harmonics, Fourier bases)?
sub_answers.text: Propagation and array responses are represented using tensorial structures that fold received data along multiple dimensions for signal processing and parameter estimation [d37768s0p0]. Beamspace representations and tensor signal models are used to capture multidimensional array characteristics and to enable interpolation or mapping of transmit arrays to desired arrays [d37768s0p0][d97529s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How is the channel matrix factorized in manifold-decomposition frameworks (e.g., decomposition into array manifold and scattering coefficients)?
sub_answers.text: Tensor decompositions such as coupled canonical polyadic decomposition express multistatic MIMO observation tensors as sums of rank-one factors that separate array manifold (Vandermonde/steering structures) from propagation amplitudes and delays [d109199s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What role do angular spectra or power angular profiles play in manifold-based channel representations?
sub_answers.text: Slowly varying angular information (angles of arrival/departure) is used to design RF stages and reduced-dimension effective channel matrices, thereby coupling manifold representations to practical beamforming and interpolation schemes [d88987s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How are basis functions chosen and truncated in practice for manifold decompositions (e.g., eigenmodes, spherical harmonics)?
sub_answers.text: Practical interpolation maps the physical array to a desired array response and truncates basis expansions to suppress out-of-sector power and reduce dimensionality for DOA estimation and beamspace design [d37768s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How do manifold-decomposition models handle multipath components, diffuse scattering, and angular spread mathematically?
sub_answers.text: Engineered scattering matrices (for example in BD-RIS designs) explicitly encode controlled propagation paths and their weights, thereby modeling multipath shaping through the scattering-matrix parameters [d123865s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Which types and magnitudes of approximation error (bias, variance, spectral leakage, aliased energy) are introduced when truncating the basis or using a finite number of modes in manifold-decomposition or modal-domain propagation models, and how do those errors scale with mode count, bandwidth, and source angular spread?
sub_answers.text: Truncating the basis or using a finite number of modes causes spectral leakage that degrades recovery accuracy in wideband channels when using fixed DFT bases [d118270s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How does using an idealized manifold assumption (for example, isotropic spherical, uniform circular, or planar wavefront models) instead of the true propagation manifold observed in urban, indoor, or maritime channels change parameter estimation accuracy and predictions of spatial correlation and received power?
sub_answers.text: Assuming idealized manifolds such as planar or uniform circular wavefronts causes degraded spectral efficiency and orthogonality when arrays are misaligned, reducing performance in practical non-parallel misalignment scenarios [d72250s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What are the quantitative compromises between adopting array-agnostic (manifold-independent) modeling approaches and capturing array-specific effects such as element mutual coupling, element pattern variability, and platform scattering — e.g., how much does ignoring coupling change beamformer output SINR, DoA bias, or Cramér–Rao bounds?
sub_answers.text: Array-agnostic models that ignore element coupling, pattern variability, and platform scattering trade physical accuracy for generality and can fail to capture SINR and beamforming gains recoverable by array-specific modeling when misalignment or element effects are significant [d72250s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How do common imperfections—additive measurement noise, finite angular sampling resolution, limited snapshot/sample counts, and discretized angular grids—impact the stability and estimation error of array-independent manifold decompositions; what are the thresholds (SNR, snapshots, angular bin width) where performance degrades significantly?
sub_answers.text: Additive measurement noise and limited time-bandwidth product affect the tightness of approximate joint-PDF factorizations, with approximation errors that become exponentially small in the number of nodes when the time-bandwidth product is sufficiently high [d80690s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What concrete steps in antenna layout optimization and decisions about port count or element spacing become easier when using array-independent channel parametrizations; cite specific design stages or metrics (e.g., mutual coupling reduction, SNR variance, pattern synthesis) that are simplified?
sub_answers.text:
Geometry optimization and port-selection decisions can be framed as continuous aperture or position optimization problems that jointly handle radiation response and multiport mutual-impedance, simplifying antenna placement and spacing tradeoffs [d128414s0p0].
Accounting for mutual coupling explicitly during layout lets designers target mutual-coupling reduction and correct transmit-power and noise calculations during array-layout choices [d52311s0p0].
Using orientation-domain degrees of freedom enables direct optimization of element boresight directions as a design stage, which simplifies pattern synthesis and SNR-variance reduction steps compared with fixed arrays [d122979s0p0].
Expressing optimal current or pattern solutions as linear combinations of channel spatial responses reduces the need for complex integration in pattern-synthesis stages and eases decisions about effective element count or port mapping [d104139s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How do manifold-based channel models change the formulation and implementation of MIMO precoding and beamforming algorithms, and what is their measurable impact on achievable rate/capacity estimates, spectral efficiency, and rank characterization under realistic propagation scenarios?
sub_answers.text:
Including manifold or orientation-domain structure converts precoding/beamforming into joint optimization problems over transmit covariance and geometric/orientation parameters, and admits specialized solvers such as eigenmode transmission with water-filling and Riemannian Frank–Wolfe for orientation optimization [d122979s0p0].
Manifold-aware formulations enable current-pattern or precoder designs that are linear combinations of channel spatial responses, which lowers algorithmic complexity for beamforming while retaining secrecy- and capacity-oriented objectives [d104139s0p0].
Using array-reconfigurable models for beamformer design yields measurable capacity and rate gains over fixed-array benchmarks in simulations, including significant capacity improvement from rotatable-antenna optimization and higher weighted secrecy sum-rate for continuous-aperture designs [d122979s0p0][d104139s0p0].
Manifold-based continuous repositioning and joint optimization approaches improve mainlobe SNR and reduce sidelobes, which translates to higher spectral-efficiency and more favorable effective channel rank in practical propagation scenarios [d128414s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Which practical channel sounding, pilot design, and parameter extraction procedures must be modified to obtain reliable array-independent manifold decompositions, and how do ground-truth measurement methods (e.g., SAGE, MUSIC, channel sounding sweeps) need to be adjusted to recover angle/delay parameters accurately?
sub_answers.text:
Channel-sounding procedures must measure or model the changing multiport mutual-impedance and radiation response associated with element displacement or orientation to enable reliable manifold decomposition [d128414s0p0].
Pilot-design and parameter-extraction workflows must incorporate EM-aware processing and constrained voltage/current estimation steps so that position- or orientation-dependent channel parameters can be recovered accurately [d128414s0p0].
Practical measurement campaigns should include controlled orientation sweeps and aperture-position sweeps and may require phase-retrieval or amplitude-to-complex-target conversion steps to produce aperture-compatible complex targets for parameter extraction [d128414s0p0][d105691s0p0].
Reliable extraction of spatial manifold components benefits from iterative EM-aware selection and continuous refinement methods, such as EM-aware OMP and voltage-constrained current optimization, during post-processing of sounding data [d128414s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: For large-scale and massive MIMO arrays, what are the quantifiable computational, storage, and real-time implementation advantages of using array-independent channel representations (e.g., reduced parameter count, faster projection/estimation, lower feedback overhead), and how do these scale with antenna count and user number?
sub_answers.text:
Representing channels via array-independent spatial responses enables designs whose optimal source/current patterns are expressible as linear combinations of those responses, which reduces computational complexity compared with full discrete integration and lowers algorithmic cost as array size grows [d104139s0p0].
Continuous-position models with EM-aware sparse selection and gradient-like refinement yield faster convergence in layout and beamforming optimizations, reducing per-iteration computation compared with exhaustive discrete-port searches [d128414s0p0].
Array-reconfigurable formulations support fewer effective parameters (e.g., spatial-response coefficients or orientation variables) and thus reduce storage and feedback overhead relative to storing full per-element channel matrices, improving scalability with antenna count and user number [d104139s0p0][d128414s0p0].
Practical optimization pipelines that use OMP plus projected adaptive updates or particle-swarm/SDR/MMSE hybrids demonstrate improved mainlobe SNR and sidelobe performance while keeping computational loads manageable for large arrays [d128414s0p0][d105691s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Describe the concept of decomposing the electromagnetic propagation environment into spatial manifolds for wireless channels; what are the components, purpose, and formal definition of a 'manifold decomposition' in channel modeling literature?
sub_answers.text: Manifold decomposition treats the electromagnetic propagation environment as a superposition of spatial manifolds that capture angular and spatial variation of fields using modal components such as plane waves or spatial EM modes [d119796s0p0][d80070s0p0]. The components of a manifold decomposition include modal basis functions that represent elementary propagation patterns and coefficients that weight those modes according to the scattering environment and array geometry [d119796s0p0][d80070s0p0]. The purpose of manifold decomposition is to provide a unified, physically consistent representation that captures subwavelength spatial correlation and both far-field and near-field (spherical-wave) effects for MIMO channels [d119796s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: List the criteria and distinguishing features that make a channel model 'array-independent' as opposed to 'array-dependent'; what model parameters, assumptions, or measured quantities change when you switch between these two classes?
sub_answers.text: An array-independent channel model separates environment-dependent propagation characteristics (for example angular spread, radiance distribution or scattering modes) from the specific antenna-array sampling and geometry [d120691s0p0][d80070s0p0]. An array-dependent model explicitly incorporates antenna layout and sampling (for example element spacing such as half-wavelength and aperture size) so that degrees of freedom and spatial correlations depend on array geometry [d80070s0p0][d16930s0p0]. Switching from array-dependent to array-independent formulations replaces array-specific parameters (element positions, sampling aperture) with environment-centric parameters (wavenumber/radiance distributions, scattering-mode coefficients or angular spreads) [d119796s0p0][d120691s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Explain how multipath scattering is modeled in physics-based MIMO channel models: what primitives (rays, clusters, scattering functions) are used, how do they map to channel transfer matrices, and what physical laws (e.g., reciprocity, superposition) are invoked?
sub_answers.text: Physics-based MIMO channel models represent multipath scattering using primitives such as plane waves, rays or aggregated clusters that correspond to dominant directions or scattering regions [d119796s0p0][d16930s0p0]. Those scattering primitives are mapped into channel transfer matrices by projecting the primitives onto modal bases or spatial EM modes, yielding a finite set of scattering channels or degrees of freedom that determine the matrix rank and coupling [d80070s0p0][d119796s0p0]. Correlated or "colored" scattering models capture statistical correlation among scattering primitives and lead to limits on the achievable degrees of freedom as a function of angular spread and array extent [d16930s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Identify the principal mathematical domains and orthonormal bases used to represent propagation manifolds (for example spherical harmonics, plane-wave/Fourier series, eigenfunction expansions); for each, state typical use cases, dimensionality, and advantages/limitations.
sub_answers.text: The plane-wave / wavenumber (spatial Fourier) basis is used to represent propagation manifolds for H-MIMO and provides a unified basis for planar apertures and far-field plane-wave components [d119796s0p0]. Spherical-wave or spherical-harmonic type representations are used when near-field or spherical propagation effects are significant and when capturing subwavelength spatial variation is required [d119796s0p0]. Eigenfunction or modal (spatial EM mode) expansions are used to quantify effective degrees of freedom and environment-dependent scattering channels in analytical DOF studies [d80070s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Explain, with mathematical expressions, how wireless channel matrices are decomposed in manifold-based frameworks — for example formulations that separate an array manifold (steering/response matrix) from propagation/scattering coefficient matrices; provide typical matrix factorizations, operator forms, and assumptions behind them.
sub_answers.text: Manifold-based frameworks represent a MIMO wireless channel as a matrix factorization that separates array-dependent response matrices (array manifold or steering matrices) from propagation or scattering coefficient matrices, typically written H = A(angles) X where A(·) is an array steering/response matrix and X contains modal or propagation coefficients [d15928s0p0][d123865s0p0].  Such decompositions are treated as fixed-rank matrix factorizations on matrix manifolds and are optimized using Riemannian quotient geometry or manifold optimization algorithms to enforce rank and structure constraints on the factors [d15928s0p0].  Practical decompositions also take the form H ≈ U Σ V^T or H ≈ F G where U,F represent basis/steering matrices and Σ,G contain singular values or scattering coefficients, and these factorizations are used to approximate an optimal fully-digital operator by products of structured matrices (e.g., analog, bit-resolution, baseband matrices) [d53597s0p0][d15928s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What are the mathematical definitions and roles of angular spectra, power angular profiles (PAPs) or angular power density functions in manifold or modal channel models; how are these functions used to parameterize the scattering operator or to compute coefficient covariance in such representations?
sub_answers.text: Angular spectra, power angular profiles (PAPs) or angular power density functions are functions that assign power or density over angle and serve as parametrizations of the scattering operator or channel angular content used to compute coefficient covariances [d123865s0p0].  The scattering matrix or operator is parameterized by angular distributions so that second-order statistics (coefficient covariance or singular-value distributions of scattering blocks) are computed from integrals or ensemble averages over these angular power density functions [d145657s0p0][d123865s0p0].  Mapping of manifold points to a Hilbert space and the induced subspaces can be used to express how angular distortions change the subspace structure that underlies these angular spectra and hence the covariance behavior [d103103s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Describe practical selection and truncation strategies for basis functions in manifold decompositions: how are eigenmodes, spherical harmonics, Fourier/Legendre basis, or array steering vectors chosen, how is modal truncation order determined (error bounds, energy capture, Ricean K, spatial coherence), and what are common numerical approaches?
sub_answers.text: Basis functions in manifold decompositions are chosen from physically motivated modal sets such as array steering vectors, eigenmodes, Fourier/spherical harmonic or Legendre bases, and practical selection amounts to representing the channel with a low-rank product of these basis matrices and coefficient matrices [d15928s0p0][d53597s0p0].  Modal truncation (fixed-rank approximation) is selected by rank or modal order that captures the dominant energy and is enforced as a fixed-rank constraint on the matrix manifold, with numerical criteria based on energy capture, effective rank, or optimization objectives solved via Riemannian gradient or trust-region methods [d15928s0p0].  Numerically, alternating factorization approaches and convex/ADMM-style solvers are used to compute the factors that approximate a target operator with a prescribed truncation or bit/structure constraints [d53597s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Provide the mathematical treatment used by manifold-decomposition models to represent multipath components, diffuse scattering, and angular spread: for example, pointwise specular terms plus continuous angular spectra, convolution with power angular profiles, scattering operator integrals, and how these contribute to the channel covariance or to the coefficient statistics.
sub_answers.text: Manifold-decomposition models represent multipath as a combination of discrete specular (pointwise) modal terms plus continuous angular spectra that enter the scattering operator as integrals over angle, and the overall scattering matrix is assembled from these block components (e.g., reflection and transmission blocks) whose singular-value statistics determine power distribution [d145657s0p0][d123865s0p0].  Diffuse scattering and angular spread are modeled via continuous power angular density functions that are convolved or integrated with basis functions to produce coefficient statistics and channel covariance entries through ensemble or integral formulations over the angular domain [d145657s0p0][d123865s0p0].  The resulting covariance or coefficient statistics are therefore determined by the modal coefficients' distributions and the singular-value or eigenvalue spectra of the scattering blocks, which are analyzed using random-matrix and manifold-based factorization tools [d145657s0p0][d15928s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Quantify the error terms introduced when truncating basis functions or using a finite number of propagation modes in manifold-decomposition (steering-vector) approximations; include bounds on truncation error, typical decay rates of neglected coefficients, and examples for common bases (Fourier, spherical harmonics, prolate spheroidal).
sub_answers.text: Truncating Fourier-extension bases yields geometric convergence in the truncation parameter N for the discrete least-squares Fourier extension, giving rapidly decreasing truncation error as N increases [d28875s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Assess how incorrect geometric or statistical assumptions about the propagation manifold (for example assuming an isotropic sphere, uniform angular power, or single-bounce surface) bias parameter estimates and beamforming performance; provide case studies contrasting assumed manifolds with measured urban/indoor/sea-surface scattering characteristics.

Characterize the compromises between array-agnostic modeling (e.g., using generic manifold bases or interpolation) and accurately capturing array-specific effects such as mutual coupling, element pattern variations, and platform scattering; specify conditions (frequency, element spacing, calibration quality) where array-independent models fail to reproduce these phenomena.
sub_answers.text: Bases whose gradients are not jointly orthogonal can introduce aliasing errors when approximating wavefronts, and alias-free performance requires bases formed by eigenfunctions of the Laplace operator that are simultaneously orthogonal in the relevant dot products [d39051s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Evaluate the robustness of array-independent manifold-decomposition methods to additive measurement noise, finite angular sampling/resolution, and limited snapshot counts; determine sensitivity curves for parameter estimation error versus SNR, angular grid density, and sample size, and identify mitigation strategies (regularization, model order selection, denoising).
sub_answers.text: Kernel expansions on equispaced Fourier grids admit explicit error bounds that separate aliasing and truncation contributions, which control sensitivity to finite angular sampling and grid density [d85474s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How do array-independent channel representations change the criteria and constraints used when optimizing antenna element placement, port count, and geometry compared with array-specific models?
sub_answers.text: Optimizing element placement shifts from fixed-array beam indices to exploiting geometry flexibility and movable-element degrees of freedom offered by flexible and fluid arrays [d122101s0p0] [d105691s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How do manifold-based channel models influence the design and selection of MIMO precoding and beamforming algorithms, and what impact do they have on predicted achievable capacity under realistic scattering scenarios?
sub_answers.text: Manifold- and orientation-aware channel models motivate beamspace and unitary transform designs that aim for sparse path resolution, making discrete Fourier transforms or learned unitary transforms central to precoding choices [d68900s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Which measurement techniques, pilot structures, and channel sounding calibration steps must be modified to obtain reliable channel estimates when using array-independent manifold decompositions instead of array-dependent parameterizations?
sub_answers.text: Model-free and manifold-inspired estimation methods replace heavy pilot requirements with learned low-dimensional representations and temporal tracking using autoencoders and LSTM to recover full channels from limited pilots [d115457s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: For large-scale and massive MIMO deployments, what reductions in computational complexity, data storage, or real-time processing requirements can be achieved by switching to array-independent channel models, and what are the trade-offs in accuracy and hardware implementation?
sub_answers.text: Beamspace processing via DFT or learned unitary transforms reduces baseband dimensionality and thereby lowers processing complexity in large-scale mmWave and terahertz systems by exploiting channel sparsity [d68900s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Explain the concept of decomposing the wireless propagation environment into separate geometric or functional components (a 'manifold decomposition'): what are its goals, typical decomposition terms (e.g., spatial, angular, delay domains), and how it simplifies channel representation for analysis and simulation?
sub_answers.text:
Decomposing the wireless propagation environment separates geometric and radio-functional components to produce a spatial representation of radio propagation called a radio radiance field (RRF) that captures spatial distribution and directionality of signals [d120691s0p0].
Typical decomposition terms include spatial, angular, delay and polarization domains that together enable a comprehensive Spatial-CSI description of the channel [d120691s0p0].
The decomposition simplifies channel representation by providing a unified spatial description that can be directly used for beamforming, delay-alignment modulation, and other massive MIMO and RIS implementations [d120691s0p0].
A plane-wave (wavenumber) decomposition provides a physically consistent basis for representing subwavelength-level spatial correlation and spherical-wave propagation, which simplifies analysis and simulation for holographic MIMO systems [d119796s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Provide a precise criterion that distinguishes array-independent channel models from array-dependent ones: what assumptions about antenna element patterns, mutual coupling, array geometry, and steering-vector parameterization are relaxed or fixed in each approach?
sub_answers.text: A unified wavenumber-domain basis replaces reliance on discrete Fourier/DFT representations that fail for subwavelength spacings, thereby providing an array-agnostic representation suitable for quasi-continuous apertures and both far-field and near-field regimes [d119796s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Describe how multipath scattering and object-based propagation are modeled in physics-driven MIMO channel models: what roles do clusters, rays, scattering functions, visibility regions, and ray-tracing outputs play in constructing the channel transfer matrix?
sub_answers.text:
Physics-driven MIMO channel models represent multipath propagation as multiple channel components or rays that can be grouped into clusters and recovered as individual components for system configuration [d80969s0p0].
Ray-tracing outputs are used to simulate realistic indoor environments and to generate channel estimates that reflect multipath geometry for security and performance studies [d5873s0p0].
The angular spread and the extent of the scattering environment determine the channel degrees of freedom and thereby influence how many multipath components effectively contribute to the channel transfer matrix [d16930s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: List and characterize the common function spaces and basis sets used to represent electromagnetic propagation manifolds (for example, spherical harmonics, plane-wave/Fourier bases, prolate spheroidal wave functions), and state when each basis is preferred (e.g., far-field vs. near-field, isotropic vs. anisotropic environments).
sub_answers.text:
Plane-wave or wavenumber-domain (spatial Fourier) bases are used to model H-MIMO channels and are preferred for representing subwavelength-level spatial correlation and spherical-wave propagation [d119796s0p0].
Classical discrete Fourier (DFT) bases are inadequate for subwavelength spacing and near-field regimes, motivating the use of continuous wavenumber or plane-wave bases instead [d119796s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Describe mathematically how MIMO channel matrices are decomposed in manifold-decomposition approaches — for example, explicit formulations that separate the array response (manifold) from propagation coefficients, and references to models like the array manifold times scattering matrix (A(θ) S A(φ)^H) or similar factorings.
sub_answers.text: Manifold-decomposition approaches model the array response as a linear superposition of elemental radiators by quantizing antennas into many Hertzian dipoles and expressing the radiated field as a linear model that depends on each dipole position and the point-source location [d90553s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What is the precise role of angular power spectra / power angular profiles (PAPs) or angle-of-arrival/angle-of-departure density functions in manifold-based channel models, and how are these angular distributions used to construct or parameterize the manifold representation (e.g., as weighting functions, covariance kernels, or PSD inputs)?
sub_answers.text: Angular distributions such as angle-of-arrival and angle-of-departure densities enter manifold-based models by parameterizing orientation-dependent channel models that modify the manifold through antenna orientation and angular-domain degrees of freedom [d122979s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: In practical implementations of manifold decompositions, which functional bases are selected (for example spherical harmonics, Fourier/DFT beams, prolate spheroidal functions, eigenmodes of the spatial covariance), what criteria guide truncation (energy capture, eigenvalue thresholds, spatial aliasing limits), and how are basis truncation errors quantified?
sub_answers.text: Common functional bases used in manifold decompositions include Fourier/DFT beam bases for uniform linear arrays and learned unitary beamspace transforms optimized for sparsity, where the DFT maps array elements to direction-associated beams [d68900s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Provide the mathematical treatments used in manifold-decomposition frameworks to represent multipath clusters, specular rays, diffuse scattering, and nonzero angular spread — for instance, how are cluster power angular spreads incorporated into the scattering coefficient statistics, how are diffuse components modeled (continuous angular spectra, correlation kernels), and how do these representations affect the resulting channel covariance/cross-correlation expressions?
sub_answers.text: Manifold frameworks represent engineered or optimized propagation via a scattering matrix that multiplies array response terms to model interactions such as RIS reflection and transmission coupling [d123865s0p0][d77259s0p0].
